methods.label: Find a repeating block
methods.explanation:
Apply the appropriate rule until a value returns:
\[
98,\ 49,\ 44,\ 22,\ 11,\ 6,\ 54,\ 27,\ 22,\ldots.
\]
The fourth term is \(22\). From there, the rules give
\[
22\longrightarrow11\longrightarrow6
\longrightarrow54\longrightarrow27\longrightarrow22.
\]
Here an even number greater than \(9\) is halved, an odd number greater than \(9\) loses \(5\), and \(6\), being less than \(10\), is multiplied by \(9\). This verifies every step of the block.

The same integer always has the same next term, so returning to \(22\) makes the entire five-term block repeat. There are three terms before the repeating part. Consequently, terms \(4\) through \(98\) contain
\[
98-3=95=19\times5
\]
terms, exactly \(19\) complete blocks. The \(98\)th term is therefore the last term of a block, \(\boxed{27}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
